references.text: The same offering regulation with two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering, for cleansing.
A parallel law concerning cleansing for women after childbirth, with the same type of offering: one dove for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering.
The priest makes atonement with a sin offering and a burnt offering to cleanse from impurity, following the same pattern as in Leviticus 15:30.
A direct parallel for men with a discharge: the priest offers one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering and makes atonement for him.
The priest makes atonement (כִפֶּר) for the sin, and the person receives forgiveness - the same principle of atonement.
The burnt offering (עֹלָה) makes atonement for the one who offers it, a fundamental principle of atonement through sacrifice.
The Nazirite brings the same type of offering after impurity: turtledoves or young pigeons for a sin offering and a burnt offering.
The cleansing rituals of the Old Testament point forward to Christ's blood that cleanses the conscience from dead works.
